summary: Tested Gastos Fijos flow end-to-end (backend + frontend). CRUD operations for fixed expenses work correctly (day_of_month + start_date persisted, listed, updated). start_date skip-generation for future dates works. However, the user-reported bug is CONFIRMED: the due_date of the auto-generated expense does NOT match the configured day_of_month. Backend generates the expense with due_date = today + 30 days (server.py line 3313), so if day_of_month = 12 and generation runs on Aug 12, the resulting expense has due_date 2026-09-11 (day 11) instead of day 12. UI verified: list shows all fields (Proveedor, Nombre, Monto, Día de cobro, Fecha Inicio, Duración, Última Generación); edit dialog loads day_of_month and start_date correctly. Dashboard 'Vencimientos a 30 días' confirms bug in production (Planilla Abril día 12 → vence 11/09/26).

critical.issue: BUG CONFIRMED: due_date is calculated as (today + 30 days) instead of using the configured day_of_month. Reproduction: create fixed expense with day_of_month = today.day and start_date <= today; run generate-now; the resulting expense has due_date.day = today.day - 1 or +/- (offset by 30 days), NOT day_of_month. Expected: due_date should be either the current day_of_month (if same month) or day_of_month of next month. Fix: replace `due_date = (today + timedelta(days=30)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')` with logic that computes the next occurrence of `fe['day_of_month']` (handling month-end clamping for days 29-31).

minor.issue: start_date is now required in FixedExpenseCreate (server.py line 504) but the test file test_fixed_expense_start_date.py has a case that expects it to be optional. Model docstring/older tests are stale.

Response does not include a `proximo_vencimiento` computed field. The requirement mentions 'cálculo automático del próximo vencimiento' but backend does not expose it (frontend does not display it either).

integration_issues.issue: The info card literally says 'se crea un nuevo gasto pendiente con vencimiento a +30 días' (GastosFijos.js line 471). This contradicts the field label 'Día de cobro mensual' which implies the day should be the due date. Either the label is misleading or the +30 days logic is wrong.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix generate_fixed_expenses_for_today in /app/backend/server.py (~line 3311-3313). Replace `due_date = today + 30 days` with computation of the actual configured day_of_month for the target month. Reference logic: `due_date_dt = today.replace(day=min(fe['day_of_month'], calendar.monthrange(today.year, today.month)[1]))`; if that date has already passed for the month, use next month.
Update UI note in /app/frontend/src/pages/GastosFijos.js line 469-471 to reflect the corrected behavior (remove '+30 días' text).
Update test_fixed_expense_start_date.py::test_create_without_start_date_allowed_optional since start_date is now required (or make it optional again in the model as originally intended).
Consider adding a computed `proximo_vencimiento` field in the FixedExpenseResponse so the frontend can show when the next expense will be generated/due.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 3515 lines long - fixed expenses logic should be moved to /app/backend/routes/fixed_expenses.py (which already exists as a stub).

generate_fixed_expenses_for_today conflates 'expense_date' (date the expense is recorded) with 'due_date' (when it must be paid). The +30 days offset applied to due_date has no relation to the configured day_of_month, which is the user's core complaint.
Duplicate FixedExpense Pydantic models exist in both server.py (line 499+) and routes/fixed_expenses.py - source of truth ambiguity.
duration_type / end_date fields exist in the DB schema but are not present in FixedExpenseCreate/FixedExpenseResponse Pydantic models (only in the DB and update path). Inconsistent contract.

generate-now endpoint applies duplicate-prevention via `last_generated` = 'YYYY-MM' string, which prevents generating twice in the same calendar month. Combined with the +30 day bug this creates confusing behavior when day_of_month is near month end.

rca of the issue: Root cause: /app/backend/server.py, function generate_fixed_expenses_for_today, line 3313: `due_date = (today + timedelta(days=30)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')`. This hard-codes a +30 day offset from the current date, completely ignoring the fe['day_of_month'] value that the user configured. Reproduction: 1) Login as superadmin. 2) Create fixed expense with day_of_month=today.day, start_date<=today. 3) POST /api/fixed-expenses/generate-now. 4) GET /api/expenses and observe due_date is today+30 (e.g. today=Aug 14 → due=Sep 13) instead of the configured day. Mitigation/Fix: `import calendar; target_month = today.month + 1 if today.day >= fe['day_of_month'] else today.month; ... clamp day to last day of month; due_date = date(target_year, target_month, min(fe['day_of_month'], calendar.monthrange(target_year, target_month)[1]))`. Also update the UI note in GastosFijos.js that promises '+30 días'.
